title: Continuatio Fragmentorum ex Adversariis mathematicis depromptorum

deep.reconstruction:
Problem (marked as Lexell's): find integers p,q,r,s such that λ(p²+s²)(q²+r²)/[pqrs(p²−s²)(q²−r²)] is a square, for a given λ. Read as a statement about Pythagorean triangles: p²+s² is the hypotenuse and ps(p²−s²) is the area of the triangle generated by (p,s), and likewise for (q,r). The condition is that (hyp₁·hyp₂)/(area₁·area₂) lies in the square class of λ.

Step I. Take p+is = (a+ib)(x−iy)-type products: p=ax+by, s=bx−ay, q=cx+dy, r=dx−cy. Then p²+s² = (a²+b²)(x²+y²) and q²+r² = (c²+d²)(x²+y²). The common factor (x²+y²)² is a square and drops out.

Step II. Impose r=s, so that rs=s² drops out. This gives x:y = (a−c):(b−d). Taking x=a−c, y=b−d gives
- p = a²−ac+b²−bd,
- q = ac−c²+bd−d²,
- r = s = ad−bc.
The condition becomes λ(a²+b²)(c²+d²)/[pq(p+s)(p−s)(q+r)(q−r)] = □.

Step III. Impose p = c²+d², which cancels p. Solve it by d=a: then c²+ac−b²+ab = (c+b)(c−b+a) = 0, so c = b−a. This gives
- p = 2a²−2ab+b², q = (3a−b)(b−a), r = s = a²+ab−b²,
- p+s = a(3a−b), p−s = (b−a)(2b−a),
- q+r = (2a−b)(2b−a), q−r = a(3b−4a).
The denominator contains the squares (3a−b)², (b−a)², a², (2b−a)². The problem therefore collapses to the binary quartic condition λ(a²+b²)(2a−b)(3b−4a) = □, which the next page states. That page also remarks that four pairs of linear factors vanished 'praeter expectationem'. It gives the companion case d=−a, and then shows by a general parametrization of p = c²+d² that the special choice d=a was in fact fully general. In modern terms the problem reduces to finding rational points on a genus-1 quartic y² = λ(a²+b²)(2a−b)(3b−4a), i.e. a quadratic twist of an elliptic curve.
errors: No mathematical errors on this page; all identities check (p, q, s=r, p±s, q±r, and the factorizations in III).
The printed final denominator has lost minus signs ('(2b  a)(2a  b)'); it should read (2b−a)(2a−b).
On the next page (not this one) q+r is printed as −a(4a+b); the correct value, consistent with the later formula, is −a(4a+3b).

ideas.what: Use the multiplicativity of sums of two squares (Brahmagupta–Fibonacci identity) to make (p²+s²)(q²+r²) a square times (a²+b²)(c²+d²)
ideas.where_published: Throughout Euler's Diophantine papers and the Algebra (E387/E388)

ideas.what: Successive specializations (r=s, p=c²+d²) chosen to turn factors into squares, reducing a degree-12 condition to a quartic λ·F(a,b)=□
ideas.modern_name: Reduction to a genus-1 curve (quadratic twist of an elliptic curve) via special subvarieties
ideas.where_published: General method in many Euler papers on λ·quartic=□; this specific problem unsure

ideas.what: Reading of the expression as (hypotenuse·hypotenuse)/(area·area) for two Pythagorean triangles generated by (p,s) and (q,r)
ideas.where_published: unsure; the attribution to Lexell suggests a problem circulated in Euler's circle

deep.surprise_reason: This is a correct, routine piece of Eulerian Diophantine analysis reducing a four-variable square condition to λ·(binary quartic)=□. The 'unexpected' cancellation of four squared factors is a pleasant computational observation but not a new result. The reduction to a twist of an elliptic curve is the standard outcome of Euler's method. The page is already published in the Opera postuma.
transcription_corrections: Final displayed denominator: image shows '(2b  a)(2a  b)' with signs lost; correct reading is (2b−a)(2a−b).
Otherwise the transcription matches the image; 's=r=ab−bc−ab+ad=ad−bc' is as printed and correct.
